service_name: Water Supply — New Connection, Reconnection & Repairs
sub_service: New domestic/ICI/bulk-meter connections, reconnection, pipe/ferrule change, tube-well installation
problem_type: Need for a new water connection, reconnection after disconnection, or pipe/ferrule repair
authority: Assistant Engineer (Water Supply) concerned, or the Director General Water Supply for bulk-meter connections
description: KMC's Water Supply Department Citizens' Charter publishes a table of 9 specific services with their own application procedure, documents required, and time limit: new connections for Industrial/Commercial/Institutional (ICI) use, new bulk-meter connections, new domestic connections, new building-construction connections, conversion of a construction connection to domestic use, reconnection of water supply, change of pipe/ferrule size, water-tanker supply, and installation or repair of new tube-wells/borewells (via the State Water Investigation Directorate, SWID).
procedure: Application form available at the KMC website; submit with required documents (e.g. trade license, KMC property tax clearance certificate, 'No Objection' certificate from the owner if the applicant is a tenant, occupancy certificate for new buildings) to the Assistant Engineer (Water Supply) concerned or the Ward Office. For new tube-wells, the permit is obtained from the State Water Investigation Directorate, Government of West Bengal, after which KMC issues the license-fee details.
required_documents: 'No Objection' certificate from the property owner (if the applicant is a tenant)
Photocopy of the building sanction plan and the building-sanction-fee payment receipt (for new building construction connections)
Plumber 'Niyog patra' / letter of authorization to a KMC-licensed plumber (for new building construction connections)
sla: New ICI connection: 4 working days from deposition of necessary charges. New bulk-meter connection: 30 working days (after a departmental inspection following application). New domestic connection: 4 working days. New building-construction connection: 4 working days. Conversion of a building-construction connection to domestic use: 4 working days. Reconnection of water supply: 24 hours. Change of pipe or ferrule size: 4 working days. Water-tanker supply: 2 (unit not specified in the source document). New tube-well/borewell: SWID issues permit-fee details within 2 working days of receiving the permit application; the license-fee receipt itself then serves as the tube-well license.
expected_response_time: 24 hours for reconnection of water supply
expected_resolution_time: 4 working days for most new/altered connections; 30 working days for a new bulk-meter connection
complaint_channel: Ward office / Assistant Engineer (Water Supply) concerned, per the published list of 21 local offices and 8 zonal Executive Engineer offices
contact_information: 21 local Water Supply offices (Assistant Engineers), each covering specific ward numbers, are published in the charter -- e.g. Cossipur Section (10, B.T. Road, Kolkata-700002, Ph: 2558 8553) covers wards 1-6; Hatibagan Section (79, Bidhan Sarani, Kolkata-700006, Ph: 2543 1602) covers wards 7-12,15. 8 zonal Executive Engineer offices are also published, e.g. E.E.(North): Hatibagan Section, 79 Bidhan Sarani, Kolkata-700006, Ph 2543 1602, covering wards 1-12, 15-28, 38, 39; E.E.(Central): 5 S.N. Banerjee Road, KMC CMO Building, Kolkata-700013, Ph 2286 1100-1109 (ext 2425), covering wards 13,14, 40-65. A dedicated Tubewell Executive Engineer covers all wards 1-141, same address/ext 2567.
escalation_procedure: 'For inquiries' and 'For complaints/suggestions' both route to the Zonal Executive Engineer concerned for the relevant local office/ward, per the published list of 21 Assistant Engineer offices and 8 Executive Engineer offices.
escalation_authority: Zonal Executive Engineer concerned (North / Central / West / South / Jadavpur / S.S. Unit / G.R. Unit / Tubewell)

faq.question: How long does a new domestic water connection take in Kolkata?
faq.answer: 4 working days from deposition of the necessary charges, per KMC's own Water Supply Citizens' Charter.

faq.question: How fast is a water-supply reconnection done?
faq.answer: Within 24 hours, per the same charter.

citizen_guidance: Water supply depends on availability of surface/ground water at a given point, and new connections may be constrained by the existing distribution network's capacity. Citizens should engage only KMC-licensed plumbers and verify their license papers.
source_title: Citizens' Charter — Water Supply Department, Kolkata Municipal Corporation

service_name: Solid Waste Management — Collection, Transport & Disposal
sub_service: Door-to-door waste collection, open-vat conversion, landfill/disposal operations
description: KMC is responsible for collection, transportation, disposal, and treatment of waste generated in the city, stated on this page as averaging 4,000 MT/day. The page is presented as a reform achievements report and appears to date from around 2009-2010 (its own tables compare 2004-05 against '2005-09' and describe a remediation project 'expected to start from April 2010') -- the specific figures below should be treated as historical/dated, not necessarily current: waste collected grew from ~2,999.5 MT/day (2004-05) to ~3,932 MT/day (2005-09 period); open-vats converted to direct loading grew from 46 to 60; door-to-door household coverage grew from 50%% to 65%%; disposal-site area grew from 21.47 to 35.5 hectares. A KMC compost plant operates at Dhapa, converting waste to fertilizer; a slaughterhouse-waste Effluent Treatment Plant (100 KLD) and a bio-composting plant were also built at Dhapa.
procedure: PROCEDURE NOT FOUND — this page describes department achievements/statistics, not a citizen complaint-lodging procedure for uncollected waste.
sla: SLA NOT FOUND — this page is a reform-achievements report (collection tonnage, coverage %, infrastructure counts) and does not state a complaint-to-resolution SLA.
contact_information: CONTACT INFORMATION NOT FOUND — no SWM-specific complaint number or office is published on this page.
citizen_guidance: This KMC page documents solid-waste infrastructure and reform achievements (collection tonnage, door-to-door coverage, disposal-site capacity) rather than a citizen complaint process -- it does not itself state how to report uncollected garbage or what response time to expect.

sub_service: Non-glowing/daytime-lit streetlights, damaged poles/wiring, missing streetlights, equipment pilferage
problem_type: Streetlight not working, streetlight on during the day, damaged pole/loose wiring (electrocution risk), no streetlight in area, suspected pilferage of lighting equipment
authority: Executive Engineer (Lighting) for the ward's zone (6 zones, each covering a named group of wards)
description: KMC's Department of Lighting handles installation and maintenance of streetlights, park/garden lighting, crematorium electrics, and institutional lighting (schools, ward offices). Its FAQ page gives concrete reporting channels: a citywide Control Room, plus 6 zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting) offices, each responsible for a specific set of boroughs/wards -- e.g. Zone 1 (Boroughs 1-3, wards 1-20 & 29-35) at 79 Bidhan Sarani, Kolkata-700006; Zone 6 (Borough 16, wards 123-126 & 142-144) at 4 Diamond Park, Joka, Kolkata-700104. Citizens are explicitly encouraged to report non-glowing/daytime-lit lights, missing streetlights, damaged poles or loose wiring (electrocution risk), and suspected pilferage of lighting equipment -- with an assurance that a pilferage reporter's identity is kept confidential.
procedure: Contact the citywide Control Room, or the Executive Engineer (Lighting) for the zone covering the citizen's ward (see the 6-zone contact table on this page).
required_information: Ward number (to identify the correct zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting))
sla: SLA NOT FOUND — the FAQ page names who to contact for each type of streetlight issue but does not state a numeric response/resolution-time commitment.
complaint_channel: Zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting) — 6 zones, contact by ward (see description)
contact_information: Control Room: (033) 2286 1212, (033) 2286 1313, (033) 2286 1414. Zone 1 (wards 1-20, 29-35): Executive Engineer (Lighting), 79 Bidhan Sarani, Kolkata-700006. Zone 2 (wards 21-28, 36-55, 60-62): 15N Neli Sengupta Sarani, Kolkata-700087. Zone 3 (wards 56-59, 63-80, 82-88, 90): 3rd Floor, 28 A.K.N Sen Road, e-Governance Building, Kolkata-700042. Zone 4 (wards 81, 89, 91-114): Santoshpur Municipal Market (1st Floor), Kolkata-700075. Zone 5 (wards 115-122, 127-141): Parnashreepally Government Quarter Block 14, Kolkata-700060. Zone 6 (wards 123-126, 142-144): 4 Diamond Park, Joka, Kolkata-700104.
escalation_procedure: ESCALATION INFORMATION NOT FOUND — the page names the responsible zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting) as the point of contact but does not state a further escalation authority or timeline.

faq.question: Who do I contact if streetlights in my area are lit in the day or not lit at night?
faq.answer: Contact the Executive Engineer (Lighting) for your zone (see the ward-to-zone contact table), or the citywide Control Room at (033) 2286 1212 / 1313 / 1414.

faq.question: My area has no streetlights at all — who do I contact?
faq.answer: The same zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting) responsible for your ward.

faq.question: What if I notice someone stealing lighting equipment?
faq.answer: Report it to the concerned zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting) — your identity is kept confidential.

faq.question: A streetlight pole is damaged with loose/exposed wiring — what do I do?
faq.answer: Contact the Lighting Department immediately via the zonal Executive Engineer (Lighting) or the Control Room.

citizen_guidance: Find your ward's zone from the 6-zone table and contact that zone's Executive Engineer (Lighting), or call the Control Room at (033) 2286 1212 / 1313 / 1414 for any streetlight issue -- not working, on during the day, missing, damaged/loose wiring, or suspected equipment theft.
source_title: Department of Lighting — FAQ & Zone Contacts

sub_service: Damage to roads/bridges/culverts/PWD buildings, bad quality materials or workmanship complaints
problem_type: Potholes, damaged roads, damaged bridges/culverts, poor-quality PWD construction work
department: Public Works Department (PWD), Government of West Bengal
description: West Bengal PWD's own grievance portal explicitly covers damages to roads, bridges, culverts and buildings belonging to PWD, and complaints about bad quality materials or bad workmanship -- confirmed by direct fetch, closing the gap left by KMC's own Roads page (confirmed unusable: only a table of completed civil-works statistics, no complaint procedure). This is state-wide PWD, covering PWD-maintained roads specifically -- West Bengal's road network is split across PWD, KMC, and KMDA by classification, matching the same jurisdiction-split pattern already documented for other states in this project.
procedure: Submit a complaint via the WhatsApp helpline with details of the road/bridge/culvert damage or workmanship issue.
sla: SLA NOT FOUND -- no numeric response/resolution time published on this page.
escalation_procedure: NOT FOUND IN OFFICIAL SOURCE on this page.
source_title: Grievance Portal — Public Works Department, West Bengal
source_organization: Public Works Department (PWD), Government of West Bengal
